text:
deploy-bot: [ALERT] Post-deploy telemetry: p95 latency steady, p99 jumped from 380ms -> 3.8s in last 3m. 5xx rate on /api/generate rose 3.2% -> 12%. Canary completed to 100% ~7m ago. Dash: https://dash.internal/redwood/alerts/1779991234

Ben (oncall): ack. paging SRE and runtime. @Carla you available?

Carla (sre): here. looking at traces -> spike correlates with increased backend TTFB and connection resets to runtime pool. Also seeing KV miss rate up 8x after deploy. pulling logs now.

Ben (oncall): any sign of customer impact yet? Maya (support) can you pull CS tickets?

Maya (support): CS has 4 separate tickets within last 10m complaining about timeouts on generation endpoints. A couple are enterprise customers hitting rate limits then timeouts. Flagging as P1 potential.

David (eng-runtime): the rollout to prod completed 7m ago. Canary to 100% was automated. Suspect a change in cache key namespace in the new runtime revision that causes higher miss and extra downstream load. Revert?

Carla (sre): metrics: redis latency spikes during burst and a handful of ECONNRESETs between proxy and runtime pods. stack: proxy -> runtime -> redis. If cache misses increased, runtime issues more DB work and stalls.

Alice (eng-platform): I can initiate a rollback. Rolling back to revision r1234 now: `/deploy rollback --env prod --to r1234`

deploy-bot: rollback initiated by Alice (eng-platform). Estimated rollback window 75-120s. Notifying CI and traffic manager.

Ben (oncall): while rollback runs, can we add temporary workarounds? Increase proxy connection pool and circuit timeouts to shed load from runtime?

David (eng-runtime): applying quick hotpatch to revert cache prefix change and triggering a targeted cache flush for the new prefix. Command running on runtime pods: ```kubectl exec -it deploy/runtime-xyz -- bash -c "python -m runtime.tools.flush_prefix --prefix newprefix:v2"```

Carla (sre): rollback complete per deploy-bot. Observed p99 drop: 3.8s -> 420ms in next minute, 5xx rate falling from 12% -> 1.1%. KV miss rate trending down. Still watching.

Maya (support): customer updates: sent an FYI to affected customers, told them we're rolling back and monitoring. Will escalate if errors persist.

Ben (oncall): good. we'll keep incident open for postmortem. Immediate mitigation = rollback + hotpatch. Next steps: root cause validation (cache key change), add canary assertion for KV miss spike, add pre-deploy cache migration/flush step, alert on sudden miss-rate > 3x baseline. @Alice @David please create follow-ups.

Alice (eng-platform): created ticket INF-4932: "prod p99 spike after deploy - cache-prefix regression". Assigned to David + Carla for RCA and tests. Link: https://issues.internal/INF-4932

David (eng-runtime): will open PR to revert change in source, add unit + integration test for key namespace, and add graceful fallback if redis returns error. ETA for PR: 3h.

Carla (sre): monitoring for 15m stabilization window. If p99 stays <600ms and 5xx <1.5% we will close the page and continue as postmortem. :white_check_mark:

Ben (oncall): Handoff: my shift ends in 30m, next oncall is Sam. I'll post summary in #sre-oncall and mark incident for follow-up.

Maya (support): will update customers with follow-up once stabilization confirmed.

Alice (eng-platform): uploading minimal rollback timeline and audit to INF-4932.

Carla (sre): incident moving to monitoring state. Keep thread for notes.

Ben (oncall): thanks team. :thumbsup:
